title: Writing into a file with ofstream

visuals.title: Where the data goes: from your program into the file

stages.name: 1. Your variables
stages.detail: Values such as roll, name and marks live in RAM while the program runs.

stages.name: 2. The stream out
stages.detail: ofstream out("students.txt"); creates a pipe from your program to the file. out << value pushes data into the pipe, just like cout << value.

stages.name: 3. The file on disk
stages.detail: The text is stored in students.txt. A plain ofstream first erases the old content; ios::app keeps it and adds at the end.

stages.name: 4. close()
stages.detail: out.close() finishes the transfer. The file stays on the disk after the program ends.

goal: After this you can write text, numbers and a whole table of records into a file, choose between overwriting and appending, and check that the file opened.
warmup: Imagine the canteen owner writing each day's sales in a register. If he starts a fresh page every morning, yesterday's page is lost for his own records. If he continues below yesterday's last line, nothing is lost. Writing into a file is the same: a plain ofstream starts a fresh page (erases), while ios::app continues below the last line.
definition: To write into a file you create an ofstream object with the file name: ofstream out("data.txt");. If the file does not exist, it is created. If it exists, its old content is erased (this is the default mode ios::out). Then you use << on out exactly as you use << on cout: numbers, text, variables and endl all work. In a text file, everything is stored as characters, so the number 78 becomes the two characters 7 and 8. When you are finished you call out.close(). To keep the old content and add at the end, open the file with ios::app: ofstream out("data.txt", ios::app);.
howItWorks: Watch the first trace: each << adds characters to the file. Notice what the program does NOT do: it does not add spaces or new lines for you. If you write out << 12 << 34, the file contains 1234, one number glued together. So put a space (or endl) between values: out << 12 << " " << 34. Always check if (!out) after opening. The open fails for example when the folder is read-only or the name is invalid. To save a whole table, use a for loop over the array of structures and write one line per record: roll, a space, name, a space, marks, endl, as in the third example. A good habit is a one-line record with the fields separated by spaces, because the next lesson shows how easily >> can read such lines back. In every sample here we read the file back at the end only to display it, so you can see what was written.

mistakes.wrong:
ofstream out("scores.txt");
out << 55 << endl;   // second run of the program
mistakes.error: No compiler error. A plain ofstream erases what was there, so only the newest score survives. Use ios::app when old data must stay.
No compiler error. The file contains 1234 (we checked it by running it): the two numbers are glued into one. Put a space between the values.

The compiler reports error: conversion from 'const char [9]' to non-scalar type 'std::ofstream' {aka 'std::basic_ofstream<char>'} requested. The file name goes inside parentheses when you create the stream.

mistakes.wrong:
ofstream out("data.txt");
cout << "Ali" << endl;   // wrong stream!
mistakes.error: No compiler error. The text appears on the screen and the file stays empty, because cout writes to the screen. Use the name of your file stream.
No compiler error. A stream also closes itself at the end of its scope, but closing it yourself shows you finished and makes sure the data is saved before you open the file again.

examTips: State the default: ofstream erases old content. ios::app appends. This is asked almost every time.
Put a space or endl between values. Output stuck together (1234) loses marks and is unreadable.
For a table of records, use a for loop over the array and write one line per record.
Write the check if (!out) after opening, and out.close() at the end.
A file name is a string in double quotes: "students.txt". Do not use a full path.
romanSummary: ofstream out("data.txt"); file ko likhne ke liye kholta hai, aur out << ... bilkul cout ki tarah kaam karta hai.
Purani file ka data mit jata hai, jab tak aap ios::app na likhein. ios::app data ko aakhir mein jorta hai.
Values ke darmiyan space ya endl zaroor likhein, warna 12 aur 34 mil kar 1234 ban jate hain.
Array of structures ko file mein likhne ke liye for loop use karein, har record ek line mein.
Kholne ke baad if (!out) se check karein aur aakhir mein out.close() karein.
